title: 2021年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 Can you remember what you ate yesterday? If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk? Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out.

P2 We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades. We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.

P3 Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.

P4 Why is this happening? We can point to at least three potential causes. One is the rise in obesity levels itself. Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.

P5 Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not. This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking".

P6 The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.

P7 So, what's the message conveyed? For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options. For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories. If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet. Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.

questions.q: What did the author suspect back in 2016?
options: Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades.
Most people surveyed were reluctant to reveal what they ate.
The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption.
Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the author suspect back in 2016 问的是一个具体过去时间点上的具体事实，没 有 infer/imply 之类信号词，属于事实细节题。 51. What did the author suspect back in 2016? A) Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades. B) Most people surveyed were reluctant to reveal what they ate. C) The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption. D) Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake.

【拆句】题干 What did the author suspect back in 2016? 是一个简单的特殊疑问句，主语 the author，谓语 suspect，宾语用 what 提问，back in 2016 是时间状语，结构平铺直叙，无 陷阱。

【定位】We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades. 我们最初是在 2016 年产生这种怀疑的——我们困惑于一个事实：国家统计数据显示，过去 几十年里热量消费在大幅下降。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades. 复述的是统计数据本 身的表象，作者恰恰是怀疑这个表象不可信，而非相信它。 B) 无中生有 原文只说人们 drastically under-reporting——漏报，没有任何文字表明他们 reluctant to reveal——主观上不愿透露；后文第 5 段更解释为自我欺骗或愿景式思维，而非拒绝 回答。 C) ✓ 正确 national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades ↔ The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption. 预判落点是“统计与现实不符”，四个选项里只有 The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption. 直接说统计没有反映真实情况，与预判完全吻合。 D) 张冠李戴 Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake. 接近第 1 段 every snack bar in your car 和第 6 段 snacking 的内容，但那些不是 2016 年的怀 疑，而是后续展开的具体机制。 国家统计局证实了什么? A) 人们的卡路里摄入量远未被准确报告。 B) 遗漏正餐导致了吃零食的习惯。 C) 国家的肥胖水平与卡路里摄入量有很大关系。 D) 卡路里摄入量与一个人吃零食的量有关。

questions.q: What has the Office for National Statistics verified?
options: People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported.
The missing out of main meals leads to the habit of snacking.
The nation's obesity level has much to do with calorie intake.
Calorie consumption is linked to the amount of snacks one eats.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has the Office for National Statistics verified? 直问某机构核实了什么事实，无推 断信号词，属事实细节题。

【拆句】题干 What has the Office for National Statistics verified? 是现在完成时的特殊疑问句， 主语是机构名，谓语 verified，结构清晰，无障碍。 52. What has the Office for National Statistics verified? A) People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported. B) The missing out of main meals leads to the habit of snacking. C) The nation's obesity level has much to do with calorie intake. D) Calorie consumption is linked to the amount of snacks one eats.

【定位】Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim. 如今国家统计局已证实：我们实际摄入的热量比国家统计声称的高出 50%。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim ↔ People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported. People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported. 把“实际比上报高出 50%” 这件事精确概括为“摄入量远未被准确上报”，与预判一一对应。 B) 无中生有 The missing out of main meals leads to the habit of snacking. 把“漏掉正餐”和“养成 吃零食的习惯”绑成因果，原文从未提及这种因果链——文中说的是“忘记零食”而非“漏掉 正餐导致吃零食”。 C) 张冠李戴 The nation's obesity level has much to do with calorie intake. 涉及肥胖与热量摄入 的关系，那是第 4 段 rise in obesity levels 后面的讨论，不是国家统计局证实的内容。 D) 张冠李戴 Calorie consumption is linked to the amount of snacks one eats. 类似第 6 段对零 食的讨论，但那是作者推论的“潜在原因之一”，不是国家统计局已证实的事实。 从文章中我们对肥胖者了解到什么? A) 他们通常对自己的饮食习惯保密。 B) 他们忽视了肥胖的潜在原因。 C) 他们情不自禁地吃得比应该吃的多。 D) 他们难以回忆起自己吃过什么。

questions.q: What do we learn about obese people from the passage?
options: They usually keep their eating habits a secret.
They overlook the potential causes of obesity.
They cannot help eating more than they should.
They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about obese people from the passage? 限定主体为某类人，问关于 他们的文本陈述，仍是文中明示的细节而非推断。

【拆句】题干 What do we learn about obese people from the passage? 是 What 引导的疑 问句，about obese people 限定 learn 的对象，from the passage 是出处状语，句意 直白。

【定位】Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember. 肥胖人群的漏报率要高得多，因为他们吃得本来就多，需要回想的食物也就更多。 53. What do we learn about obese people from the passage? A) They usually keep their eating habits a secret. B) They overlook the potential causes of obesity. C) They cannot help eating more than they should. D) They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 They usually keep their eating habits a secret. 把客观上的漏报误读成主观上对外保 密，原文没有任何表示故意隐瞒的字眼。 B) 张冠李戴 They overlook the potential causes of obesity. 把“忽视肥胖原因”安到肥胖人群头 上，但全文中“指出潜在原因”的是作者（We can point to at least three potential causes），与肥胖人群无关。 C) 过度推断 They cannot help eating more than they should. 加入了 cannot help（情不自禁） 和 more than they should（超出应吃的量）两个主观限制，原文只是说 simply consume more food——“就是吃得多些”，并未涉及自控力或应有量。 D) ✓ 正确 they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember ↔ They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten. 预判落在“记不清吃了什么”，四个选项中只有 They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten. 直接说回忆困难，与预判完美对应。 在食物消费调查中什么常常被忽视? A) 外出就餐的增长趋势。 B) 吃零食的潜在原因。 C) 人们的家庭能源消耗。 D) 人们多年来不断变化的饮食。

questions.q: What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption?
options: The growing trend of eating out.
The potential causes of snacking.
People's home energy consumption.
People's changing diet over the years.
questions.explain:
【判型】What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption? 问的是调查中常被漏掉 的某个具体类别，属于事实细节而非推断。

【拆句】题干 What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption? 主语 what，goes unnoticed 是系表结构（go + 形容词，表“处于…状态”），in surveys on food consumption 是地点状语限定情境，结构无陷阱，关键要识别 go unnoticed 的固定搭配 含义。

【定位】Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys. 再者，有证据表明：在家以外吃的东西，是调查中被记得最差的类别之一。 54. What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption? A) The growing trend of eating out. B) The potential causes of snacking. C) People's home energy consumption. D) People's changing diet over the years.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 food consumed out of the home ↔The growing trend of eating out. an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades ↔ The growing trend of eating out. 段末明确说在家外吃饭是漏报最严重的类别之一，只有 The growing trend of eating out. 把“外出就餐”作为答案给出，与定位句完全对应。 B) 答非所问 题干问“调查中常被漏掉的是什么”，The potential causes of snacking. 谈的是“吃零食 的潜在原因”，方向跑偏；且原文也没说零食的“原因”被漏报。 C) 偷换概念 People's home energy consumption. 字面上像“家庭能源消费”，与“在家吃饭”完全是 两个领域；原文谈的是 energy intake（能量摄入），不是 energy consumption（能 源消费）。 D) 以偏概全 People's changing diet over the years. 用“饮食习惯随年份变化”这种大词把整篇主旨 偷换上来，原文段落讲的是某一类食物在调查中被漏报，不是泛泛“饮食变化”。 作者建议政策制定者就肥胖问题采取什么措施? A) 提醒人们减少吃零食。 B) 确保人们吃不增肥的食物。 C) 确保人们不会错过正餐。 D) 确保人们不坚持同样的饮食。

questions.q: What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity?
options: Remind people to cut down on snacking.
Make sure people eat non-fattening food.
Ensure people don't miss their main meals.
See that people don't stick to the same diet.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity? 问作者对决策者的具体 建议，文中尾段已明示，属细节题而非主旨题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity? 是 What 引导的 疑问句，谓语 suggest 后接的是省略 that 的宾语从句 policymakers do ...，从句动词用原 形 do（suggest 类动词的虚拟语气），about obesity 限定建议主题。

【定位】Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. 此外，我们应当寻找新方法，确保人们吃下去的东西不会对腰围产生多大影响。 55. What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity? A) Remind people to cut down on snacking. B) Make sure people eat non-fattening food. C) Ensure people don't miss their main meals. D) See that people don't stick to the same diet.

【选项】A) 无中生有 Remind people to cut down on snacking. 让人们少吃零食，仅来自 snacking and eating out 的现象描述，文中并未在 P7 提出“提醒减少零食”这一具体政策建议。 B) ✓ 正确 what people eat wouldn\'t have much impact on their waistlines ↔ Make sure people eat non-fattening food. Make sure people eat non-fattening food. 把“吃了不会胖到腰围”换说成“吃不发胖的 食物”，是从定位句的反向角度切入同一件事——与预判正对。 C) 与原文相反 Ensure people don\'t miss their main meals. 让人们别漏掉正餐，与全文主旨方向相 反——文章说人们漏报、吃得多，不是吃得少，更不存在“应该多吃几顿正餐”的建议。 D) 偷换概念 See that people don\'t stick to the same diet. 让人们不要长期保持同一种饮食，原 文从未提及对单一饮食的看法；唯一相关的 stick to a diet 谈的是减肥者难以坚持节 食，与让大众放弃单一饮食毫无关系。
